questions.topic: Cortex: Profiles, Policy Rules, and Optimization
questions.explanation: The source states: "Navigate to Settings > Configurations > General > Agent Configurations and enable the Informative BTP Alerts and Enable Minor Content Version Updates to ensure you will stay up to date with the latest threat intelligence."

questions.question: Cortex uses WebSocket to deliver server-initiated actions to agents. What happens if the WebSocket session fails?
options: The action is immediately canceled and logged as Failed.
The action is queued and retried when a new WebSocket connection is established within 60 seconds.
The action is sent at the next agent HTTP heartbeat.
The action escalates to an email notification to the SOC team.
correct_answers: The action is sent at the next agent HTTP heartbeat.
questions.correct_answer: The action is sent at the next agent HTTP heartbeat.
questions.explanation: When a WebSocket session fails, Cortex falls back to HTTP-based agent-initiated heartbeats. The action is delivered the next time the agent checks in via heartbeat rather than being canceled or immediately retried over WebSocket.

questions.question: An analyst right-clicks a completed quarantine entry in the Action Center and selects "Restore." What is the purpose of this follow-up action?
options: It permanently deletes the quarantined file from the endpoint and archives the action.
It moves the file from quarantine back to its original location on the endpoint.
It re-quarantines the file with an updated hash signature.
It submits the file to WildFire for a new verdict before releasing it.
correct_answers: It moves the file from quarantine back to its original location on the endpoint.
questions.correct_answer: It moves the file from quarantine back to its original location on the endpoint.
questions.explanation: The Restore follow-up action undoes a quarantine by moving the file back to its original path on the endpoint. It does not delete, re-quarantine, or resubmit the file.

questions.question: A security administrator wants to ensure that all hashes on the block list are enforced even on endpoints whose malware profile is set to Report mode. Which setting must be enabled?
questions.correct_answer: Override Report Mode
questions.explanation: The Override Report Mode option, available on the Block List page under Action Center, causes the agent to block hashes on the block list regardless of whether the malware profile is configured to Report. Without this setting, profile settings take precedence.

questions.question: Which two capabilities can be disabled on an endpoint using the "Disable Capabilities" option? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Disable Capabilities dialog presents three options: Live Terminal, File Retrieval, and Script Execution. Agent Upgrade and Malware Scan are not listed in this dialog. Importantly, once disabled, these capabilities can only be restored by uninstalling and reinstalling the agent.

questions.question: An action appears in the All Actions table with the status "Completed with Partial Success." What does this status indicate?
options: The action ran successfully on all endpoints but generated warnings on some.
The action was completed on at least one endpoint but failed on others.
The action was successfully completed on some endpoints but has not yet run on the rest.
The action timed out before all targeted endpoints could start running it.
correct_answers: The action was successfully completed on some endpoints but has not yet run on the rest.
questions.correct_answer: The action was successfully completed on some endpoints but has not yet run on the rest.
questions.explanation: "Completed with Partial Success" means the action finished successfully on some endpoints, while it did not complete (or failed) on the remaining targeted endpoints. It is distinct from "Failed," which means all endpoints failed, and from "Expired," which applies before any endpoint starts.

questions.question: Within Live Terminal, which interface would an analyst use to suspend a suspicious running process on a connected endpoint?
questions.correct_answer: Task Manager
questions.explanation: Task Manager in Live Terminal is specifically designed for process investigation and management, including the ability to terminate, suspend, or resume processes. File Explorer handles file and folder management, not process control.

questions.question: A Cortex XDR response action on a Linux endpoint is configured so that if the agent loses connection to the managing server for longer than a defined period, isolation is automatically canceled. Where is this setting configured?
options: Investigation & Response > Response > Action Center > Isolate
Endpoints > Policy Management > Prevention > Profiles > Agent Settings (Linux)
Inventory > Endpoints > All Endpoints > Endpoint Control
correct_answers: Endpoints > Policy Management > Prevention > Profiles > Agent Settings (Linux)
questions.correct_answer: Endpoints > Policy Management > Prevention > Profiles > Agent Settings (Linux)
questions.explanation: The Linux-specific isolation cancellation setting (auto-cancel if the agent loses server connection after a defined period) is found within the Agent Settings profile under the Linux profiles section in Prevention Profiles, not in the Action Center or Access Management.

questions.question: The Files Retrieval action in the Action Center allows an analyst to download files from a targeted endpoint. What is the maximum number of files that can be downloaded from a single endpoint per action?
questions.explanation: Per the Action Center actions table, the Files Retrieval action allows downloading up to 20 files from each targeted endpoint per action. This limit applies per endpoint, so a bulk action against multiple endpoints can retrieve up to 20 files from each.

questions.question: An analyst selects the "Follow" checkbox in the Work Plan view. What does this option do?
options: It assigns the playbook to the analyst for exclusive editing.
It allows the analyst to observe the playbook running in real time.
It locks the playbook so no other analyst can modify tasks while it is running.
It schedules the playbook to rerun automatically when any task fails.
correct_answers: It allows the analyst to observe the playbook running in real time.
questions.correct_answer: It allows the analyst to observe the playbook running in real time.
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: The Follow checkbox in the Work Plan toolbar enables real-time visualization of the playbook as it runs, allowing analysts to watch task progress live. It does not grant exclusive access, lock the playbook, or trigger automatic reruns.

questions.question: A playbook task displays a white diamond on a violet square icon. What type of task does this represent?
options: Manual Task requires analyst intervention to mark complete
Sub-Playbook Task a nested playbook within the parent
Data Collection Task collects input through a multi-question survey
Conditional Task used as a decision tree in the playbook flow
correct_answers: Conditional Task used as a decision tree in the playbook flow
questions.correct_answer: Conditional Task used as a decision tree in the playbook flow
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: The white diamond on a violet square is the icon for a Conditional Task, which functions as a decision tree with branching logic (e.g., TRUE/FALSE paths). A manual task uses a blue arrow alone, a sub-playbook has its own sub-playbook icon, and a data collection task shows a white speech bubble on an aqua square.

questions.question: A playbook fails because a third-party threat intelligence API temporarily exceeded its rate limit. After the service recovers, which Work Plan option should the analyst use to resume without losing previously completed task results?
options: Change the Playbook replace the current playbook with the same one to restart from scratch
Run Again rerun the currently assigned playbook
Reopen Task reopen only the failed task to retry just that step
Export Playbook export the current state as a PNG for documentation
correct_answers: Run Again rerun the currently assigned playbook
questions.correct_answer: Run Again rerun the currently assigned playbook
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: The Run Again button reruns the currently assigned playbook and is specifically designed for situations where a temporary condition—such as a service outage or API rate limit—caused one or more automated steps to fail. Changing the playbook removes all completed tasks. Reopen Task is a per-task action, not a playbook-level rerun.

questions.question: When a playbook analyst needs to run the `!getInvPlaybookMetaData` command to troubleshoot performance, where must this command be entered?
options: The Playbooks page free-text search bar
The Work Plan toolbar command field
questions.correct_answer: The Case War Room
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: The `!getInvPlaybookMetaData caseid=<ID> minSize=<KB>` command is executed from the Case War Room on the Cases page. It returns task inputs and outputs, storage usage, and task type metadata to help troubleshoot playbook performance issues.

questions.question: An organization wants to collect data from external users through a survey embedded in a playbook, without requiring those recipients to authenticate. Which task type supports this use case?
options: Standard Task with an API integration input
Conditional Task with an SSO-protected form
Section Header Task with a linked external URL
questions.correct_answer: Data Collection Task
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: Data Collection Tasks host a survey on an external site that does not require authentication, allowing recipients to respond without restriction. The responses can then be used as inputs for subsequent playbook tasks. Communication Tasks (a subtype supporting SSO auth) require authentication, which is the opposite of this requirement.

questions.question: Which indicator extraction mode makes extracted data available within the issue context but NOT immediately usable as task inputs or outputs during execution?
options: None indicators are not extracted automatically
Inline extraction runs synchronously and findings are added to context data
Out-of-Band extraction runs asynchronously in parallel with other actions
Manual extraction is triggered on demand from the CLI
correct_answers: Out-of-Band extraction runs asynchronously in parallel with other actions
questions.correct_answer: Out-of-Band extraction runs asynchronously in parallel with other actions
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: Out-of-band extraction runs asynchronously (in parallel with other actions). The data becomes available within the issue but cannot be used in real-time task inputs or outputs because it is not yet available when those tasks execute. Inline extraction is synchronous and immediately available in context.

questions.question: A playbook developer wants to convert a date field from a non-Unix timestamp format to Unix format before passing it to the next task. Which Cortex feature handles this transformation?
options: Filters extract relevant data based on attribute conditions
Transformers convert or render values, including date format conversions
Playbook Inputs supply data elements from the issue or integrations
Extend Issue Context populate custom issue fields via the Advanced tab
correct_answers: Transformers convert or render values, including date format conversions
questions.correct_answer: Transformers convert or render values, including date format conversions
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: Transformers in Cortex focus on converting or rendering values. The Date transformer category specifically handles format conversions such as non-Unix to Unix. Filters extract data by matching conditions; they do not convert values. The Extend Issue Context field populates issue fields rather than transforming data types.

questions.question: The default indicator extraction mode for Tasks (applied to task results) differs from the default for Case Creation. What are these two defaults, respectively?
questions.correct_answer: Tasks: None; Case Creation: Inline
questions.topic: Cortex: Work Plan and Playbook Tasks
questions.explanation: Per the Indicator Extractor Defaults table, the default for Tasks is None (indicators are not automatically extracted from task results), while the default for Case Creation is Inline (extraction runs synchronously). Case Field Change defaults to Out-of-band, and Manual CLI commands also default to Out-of-band.

questions.question: Cortex automatically binds a newly arrived issue to an existing case using a four-step process. What happens in step 3 ("Bind") if a matching case IS found?
options: A new case is always created regardless, and the new issue is added to it.
The issue's cyber attributes are averaged with the case's existing cyber attributes and the issue is linked to the matching case.
The issue is placed in a pending queue until an analyst confirms the match manually.
The issue is merged with the highest-weight matching issue already in the case.
correct_answers: The issue's cyber attributes are averaged with the case's existing cyber attributes and the issue is linked to the matching case.
questions.correct_answer: The issue's cyber attributes are averaged with the case's existing cyber attributes and the issue is linked to the matching case.
questions.explanation: When a matching case is found, Cortex binds the issue to that case. The issue's cyber attributes then contribute to and become part of the case's cyber attributes—conceptually an "averaging" across all in-case issue attributes. A new case is only created when no matching case is found or when the existing case has reached its issue threshold.

questions.question: Which severity levels of issues can trigger the creation of a new Cortex case? (Choose two.)
options: Low (from analytics detectors with an exception)
correct_answers: Low (from analytics detectors with an exception)
questions.explanation: Only medium, high, or critical issues lead to new case creation. Informational issues do not. Low-severity issues are a special exception: only those generated by specific analytics detectors can trigger case creation, making "Low from analytics detectors" the notable low-severity case.

questions.question: An analyst notices that a case has the same Case ID (2594) associated with two different Issue IDs. What explains this grouping?
options: The issues were manually merged by a senior analyst into a single case.
Cortex detected that both issues share cyber attributessuch as the same causality instance IDand bound them to the same case.
Both issues share the same alert source, which is the sole criterion for case binding.
The issues exceeded the recurring-issue threshold and were automatically aggregated.
correct_answers: Cortex detected that both issues share cyber attributessuch as the same causality instance IDand bound them to the same case.
questions.correct_answer: Cortex detected that both issues share cyber attributessuch as the same causality instance IDand bound them to the same case.
questions.explanation: Cortex groups related issues into the same case based on shared cyber attributes (security-related attributes such as causality instance ID, IP address, domain, filename, or process name). The causality instance ID (CID) is explicitly shown as an example of a cyber attribute that places multiple issues in the same case.

questions.question: The Issues & Insights tab displays issues in two sub-tables—Issues and Insights. How does Cortex differentiate which issues appear in each sub-table?
options: Issues shows only open issues; Insights shows resolved or archived issues.
Issues shows high and medium severity issues; Insights shows low and informational severity issues.
Issues shows externally sourced alerts; Insights shows internally generated analytics detections.
Issues shows stitched causality-chain issues; Insights shows unstitched issues.
correct_answers: Issues shows high and medium severity issues; Insights shows low and informational severity issues.
questions.correct_answer: Issues shows high and medium severity issues; Insights shows low and informational severity issues.
questions.explanation: The Issues sub-table displays only high and medium severity issues, while the Insights sub-table shows low and informational severity issues. Insights are defined as a type of issue—specifically those at lower severity levels that provide contextual information rather than direct threat notifications.

questions.question: A case has accumulated a very large number of issues—far more than other active cases. How does Cortex prevent this case from "starving" other cases of new issues?
options: Cortex auto-archives the case and creates a fresh replacement case to continue receiving issues.
Cortex splits the case into two cases once it exceeds 500 issues.
Cortex auto-limits the number of issues per case to a predefined threshold (1,000 issues).
Cortex lowers the cyber attribute match weight for the oversized case, reducing its future match probability.
correct_answers: Cortex auto-limits the number of issues per case to a predefined threshold (1,000 issues).
questions.correct_answer: Cortex auto-limits the number of issues per case to a predefined threshold (1,000 issues).
questions.explanation: To prevent starvation—where one large case absorbs all new matching issues and prevents other cases from receiving them—Cortex limits each case to 1,000 issues. When this limit is reached, a new case is generated even if the incoming issue matches the existing case. This limit does not apply to manually moved issues.

questions.question: SmartScore requires which prerequisite to be enabled in Cortex Settings before it can calculate case scores?
options: SAML SSO with an external identity provider
questions.correct_answer: Cortex Analytics
questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that SmartScore "requires Cortex Analytics to be enabled in Settings." Without this, Cortex cannot compute the AI/ML-based intelligent scores that factor context analysis, case-level features, statistical prevalence, and model sub-scores.

questions.question: A scoring rule hierarchy has Root at the top. Rule10 (criteria: HOST=winpoint1, score=25) is a child of Root, and Rule11 (criteria: CATEGORY=Malware, score=10) is a child of Rule10. An incoming issue matches both rules. What is the total score applied to the issue?
options: 25 only the highest-scoring matching rule is applied
10 only the leaf (most-specific) rule in the hierarchy applies
35 both matching rules score the issue, and sub-rules are evaluated only if the parent matched
0 sub-rule scores are withheld until the case is manually reviewed
correct_answers: 35 both matching rules score the issue, and sub-rules are evaluated only if the parent matched
questions.correct_answer: 35 both matching rules score the issue, and sub-rules are evaluated only if the parent matched
questions.explanation: When an issue matches multiple scoring rules in the hierarchy, it is scored by every matching rule. Sub-rules (like Rule11/Rule2) are evaluated only if their parent rule (Rule10/Rule1) first matches. In the example, Rule1 scores 25 and Rule2 adds 10, for a total of 35 applied to the issue.

questions.question: An analyst wants to review the chronological sequence of when specific issues were added to a case and what actions were taken. Which tab in the case Details pane provides this view?
questions.correct_answer: Timeline
questions.explanation: The Timeline tab provides a chronological view of case-related issues and actions taken since the case was created, including when specific issues were added to the incident. The Executions tab shows causality chain graphs, while Issues & Insights lists current issues. Key Assets & Artifacts focuses on hosts, users, and attack actors.

questions.question: A Cortex instance has 142 datasets. An XQL query is submitted with no explicit dataset stage. Against which dataset does the query execute?
options: The dataset with the most recent log update time
The `email_data` dataset, which is the default for all query types
The `xdr_data` dataset, the only one configured as Default Query Target by default
All 142 datasets simultaneously, with results merged
correct_answers: The `xdr_data` dataset, the only one configured as Default Query Target by default
questions.correct_answer: The `xdr_data` dataset, the only one configured as Default Query Target by default
questions.explanation: By default, only `xdr_data` has the Default Query Target field set to Yes. An XQL query that omits a dataset stage runs against this default. Any dataset can be set as the default via the right-click "Set as default" action, but `xdr_data` is the out-of-box default.

questions.question: A security engineer creates a dataset using an XQL query with a `target` stage that stores query results. What dataset type does Cortex assign to this dataset?
questions.correct_answer: User
questions.explanation: User datasets are specifically created by XQL queries that use a target stage to store their results in a new dataset. System datasets are created by Cortex itself. Raw datasets come from data sources like Broker VM applets. Correlation datasets are created by Cortex Correlation rules.

questions.question: An administrator attempts to delete a System dataset from the Datasets table. What will happen?
options: The system dataset is deleted after a 24-hour grace period to allow log re-ingestion.
The delete action is not available for System datasets it does not appear in the right-click menu.
The delete action appears but fails immediately because system datasets are locked.
The delete succeeds only if the dataset has no data within the hot storage range.
correct_answers: The delete action is not available for System datasets it does not appear in the right-click menu.
questions.correct_answer: The delete action is not available for System datasets it does not appear in the right-click menu.
questions.explanation: The dataset actions availability table in the source shows that System datasets do NOT have the Delete (or Download) option; only View Schema and Set as default are available. Lookup datasets have all four actions. User/Raw datasets have View Schema, Set as default, and Delete, but not Download.

questions.question: Which file formats can be uploaded to Cortex as Lookup datasets? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Lookup dataset upload feature accepts CSV, TSV (tab-separated value), or JSON formatted files up to 30 MB. XML and YAML are not listed as supported formats. The dataset name defaults to the filename but can be changed before saving.

questions.question: A Cortex administrator wants to restrict a custom role so that analysts with that role can only query a specific subset of datasets. What must the administrator do first before selecting individual datasets for that role?
options: Create a new Lookup dataset to serve as the access scope container.
Set the selected datasets as non-default query targets to prevent unauthorized access.
Enable the "Enable dataset access management" toggle within the Datasets tab of the role configuration.
Contact Palo Alto Networks support to unlock granular dataset RBAC controls.
correct_answers: Enable the "Enable dataset access management" toggle within the Datasets tab of the role configuration.
questions.correct_answer: Enable the "Enable dataset access management" toggle within the Datasets tab of the role configuration.
questions.explanation: By default, RBAC on datasets is not enabled and all users can access all datasets. To restrict access, an administrator must enable the "Enable dataset access management" switch in the Datasets tab when creating or editing a custom role. Only after toggling this on does the interface expose the per-dataset checkbox selections.

questions.question: A Cortex engineer wants to test what a new parsing rule will do to incoming data before committing it to production. Which tool on the Parsing Rules page enables this pre-deployment evaluation?
options: The Default Rules tab, which previews rule behavior against sample logs
The Schema Viewer, which validates field mappings before ingestion
The Simulate section, which generates log output based on selected vendor-associated logs
The XQL Query Builder, which runs a test query against the `unknown_unknown_raw` dataset
correct_answers: The Simulate section, which generates log output based on selected vendor-associated logs
questions.correct_answer: The Simulate section, which generates log output based on selected vendor-associated logs
questions.explanation: The Parsing Rules page includes a Simulate section (also accessible via the Simulate tab). After selecting a user-defined rule and specifying vendor-associated logs, clicking Simulate generates output so the engineer can verify results before the rule is applied to real ingested data. This is the recommended first step in the parsing rule creation workflow.

questions.question: A raw dataset named `panw_network_mapper_raw` appears in the Datasets table. Which component generates data for this specific dataset?
options: The XDR Collector installed on Windows endpoints
The Broker VM Network Mapper application
The Cortex Analytics engine when scanning for network anomalies
The WildFire integration when analyzing network-originated file hashes
correct_answers: The Broker VM Network Mapper application
questions.correct_answer: The Broker VM Network Mapper application
questions.explanation: The source explicitly states that `panw_network_mapper_raw` is generated by the Broker VM Network Mapper application. Raw dataset names follow the `<product>_<vendor>_raw` naming convention. The `unknown_unknown_raw` dataset is a separate raw dataset for unresolved logs with undefined product/vendor attributes.

questions.question: A compliance officer needs long-term log storage for audit purposes and wants to minimize cost. The logs do not need to be fully searchable, but must still be queryable. Which Cortex storage type meets these requirements?
options: Hot Storage fully searchable but the most expensive tier
Cold Storage cheaper, still searchable but with limited search capabilities
Archive Storage completely offline, lowest cost, no search capability
Lookup Dataset Storage optimized for structured reference data queries
correct_answers: Cold Storage cheaper, still searchable but with limited search capabilities
questions.correct_answer: Cold Storage cheaper, still searchable but with limited search capabilities
questions.explanation: Cold Storage is described as a cheaper storage type often used for long-term compliance needs. Data in cold storage is still searchable but has limited search capabilities compared to Hot Storage, which is fully searchable. The source does not describe an "Archive" or "Lookup Dataset Storage" tier for raw log retention.

questions.question: SmartScore functionality is exclusively supported for cases within which Cortex domain?
options: Any domain where Cortex Analytics is enabled
questions.correct_answer: Security Domain
questions.explanation: The source states that "SmartScore functionality is exclusively supported for cases within the Security Domain." IT and Hunting domains do not support SmartScore. While SmartScore relies on Cortex Analytics, that prerequisite does not extend SmartScore to non-Security domains.

questions.question: An organization creates a new Issue Starring rule and an Issue Exclusion rule, and the same incoming issue matches both rules. Which rule takes precedence?
options: The Issue Starring rule always takes precedence because starring occurs at ingestion time.
The Issue Exclusion rule takes precedence over the Issue Starring rule.
Both rules are applied simultaneously, and the issue is starred and excluded.
The rule with the lower Star ID or Exclusion ID number takes precedence.
correct_answers: The Issue Exclusion rule takes precedence over the Issue Starring rule.
questions.correct_answer: The Issue Exclusion rule takes precedence over the Issue Starring rule.
questions.explanation: The source explicitly notes: "An Issue Exclusions rule takes precedence over an Issue Starring rule if the same issue matches both." This means an issue that would be starred is instead excluded if an exclusion rule also applies.

questions.question: A SOC engineer is creating a new Layout Rule and finds that an incoming issue does not match any of the 17 configured rules. What does Cortex do with this issue's layout?
options: The issue is held in a pending state until an analyst manually selects a layout.
The issue inherits the layout of the most recently modified rule.
The issue is assigned the Default layout, which acts as a safety net for all unmatched issues.
Cortex generates an alert notifying the administrator that no matching layout rule exists.
correct_answers: The issue is assigned the Default layout, which acts as a safety net for all unmatched issues.
questions.correct_answer: The issue is assigned the Default layout, which acts as a safety net for all unmatched issues.
questions.explanation: Layout rules are evaluated sequentially until a match is found. When no rule matches, the Default layout is applied as a safety net ensuring all issues receive a basic level of organization. The source describes the Default layout as "fundamental" to system integrity.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring notification forwarding and wants to send Management Audit Logs to an external syslog receiver. Which navigation path leads to the notification forwarding configuration in the Cortex console?
options: Investigation & Response > Response > Action Center > Notifications
Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues > Forwarding
Settings > Configurations > Object Setup > Issues > Layout Rules > Notifications
questions.correct_answer: Settings > Configurations > General > Notifications
questions.explanation: The source states: "To configure notification forwarding, you can access the Settings menu, navigate to Configurations, and select General, followed by Notifications." Log types available for forwarding include Issues, Agent Logs, Management Audit Logs, and Data Ingestion Health.

questions.question: A Cortex administrator wants to create a custom domain. Before doing so, what does the documentation specifically recommend?
options: Disable all existing built-in domains to avoid conflicts with the new custom domain.
Export all current playbook triggers to ensure they are compatible with the new domain.
Review the built-in domain options first, as custom domains might not be supported by all content.
Obtain approval from Palo Alto Networks support before activating any custom domain.
correct_answers: Review the built-in domain options first, as custom domains might not be supported by all content.
questions.correct_answer: Review the built-in domain options first, as custom domains might not be supported by all content.
questions.explanation: The source includes a Note: "Before adding a custom domain, review the built-in options. Custom domains might not be supported by all content." This warning is specific to custom domains and is not a requirement for built-in domains, which have consistent content pack support.

questions.question: Cortex Marketplace Packs, such as the "Core – Investigation and Response Pack," contain which types of domain-related content that can be implemented out of the box? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The source states that Cortex Marketplace Packs contain content such as "Playbook Triggers, Primary Playbooks, and Sub-Playbooks." Dataset Views and Case Scoring rules are configured separately in Settings and Case Configuration respectively, and are not listed as Marketplace Pack content types.

questions.question: An analyst is reviewing the Issues table filtered by Starred status. A star (★) icon appears next to an issue name. From which configuration area are the rules that produced this starring behavior managed?
options: Configurations > Object Setup > Issues > Layout Rules
Cases and Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
Cases and Issues > Case Configuration > Automation Rules
correct_answers: Cases and Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
questions.correct_answer: Cases and Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
questions.explanation: Issue starring rules are created and managed at Cases and Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues. The "Add Starring Configuration" button in this section lets administrators define filter-based criteria that star and prioritize matching issues. Layout Rules govern display layouts, not starring.

questions.question: After an administrator assigns a management scope to a user under Scoped Based Access Control (SBAC), what changes about that user's access compared to the default behavior?
options: The user loses the ability to create new layout rules until the scope is re-approved.
The user can now access child tenant datasets directly from the parent tenant.
The user can manage only the specific tags and their associated entities predefined within that scope, rather than all tags.
The user is automatically granted Instance Administrator privileges for the scoped tag family.
correct_answers: The user can manage only the specific tags and their associated entities predefined within that scope, rather than all tags.
questions.correct_answer: The user can manage only the specific tags and their associated entities predefined within that scope, rather than all tags.
questions.explanation: By default, all users have management access to all tags in the tenant. Once an administrator assigns a management scope to a user (via Settings > Configurations > Access Management > Users > Update User > Scope tab), the user can only manage the specific tags and their associated entities within that assigned scope. Scopes do not grant elevated administrator privileges.

questions.question: Which issue-related object is described as "the process identified as root cause of an attack"?
questions.correct_answer: Causality Group Owner
questions.explanation: The Causality Group Owner (CGO) is defined specifically as the process identified as the root cause of an attack — the initiator. It is available only with XDR Pro endpoints, not in the base license tier.

questions.question: A stitched issue differs from a standard issue in which way?
options: It combines two or more cases into a single container.
It is automatically correlated with logs to provide better attack visibility.
It combines two or more issues that share the same External ID.
It is an issue enhanced by an analyst through manual log review.
correct_answers: It is automatically correlated with logs to provide better attack visibility.
questions.correct_answer: It is automatically correlated with logs to provide better attack visibility.
questions.explanation: A stitched issue is an issue enhanced by Cortex that is automatically correlated with logs, providing better attack visibility. Stitched issues require XDR Pro endpoints and are distinct from manually combined issues or cases.

questions.question: When you need to view an issue's full attribute data in JSON format, which action do you use from the Issues table shortcut menu?
questions.correct_answer: Debug Issue
questions.explanation: Pressing Alt and right-clicking an issue opens a shortcut menu. Selecting "Debug Issue" opens a dialog that displays all issue attributes in JSON format (with both JSON View and Tree View options). The other options do not expose raw JSON attribute data.

questions.question: An issue's External ID is hidden by default in the Issues table. Where must an analyst go to make that column visible?
options: Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Featured Fields
questions.correct_answer: The Layout Manager
questions.explanation: The External ID column is hidden by default. It can be enabled through the Layout Manager. When the source is the Cortex XDR agent, the External ID is known as the prevention ID and corresponds to a subfolder in the Prevention folder on the endpoint.

questions.question: Which two options are considered Featured Issue Fields in Cortex? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The featured issue fields are Host, User, and IP Address. They allow analysts to add specific values (e.g., a list of critical hostnames) so those issues can be sorted or filtered to the top of the Issues table. Severity and Category are standard attributes but are not featured issue fields.

questions.question: What happens when an issue matches both an exclusion rule and a starring rule simultaneously?
options: Both rules trigger simultaneously, and the issue is starred and excluded.
Neither rule triggers; the issue is placed in a pending state.
The starring rule takes precedence, and the issue is starred.
The exclusion rule takes precedence over the starring rule.
correct_answers: The exclusion rule takes precedence over the starring rule.

questions.question: Under the "Retrieve Additional Data" right-click option, which sub-option initiates retrieval of attack-related executables from an endpoint?

questions.explanation: "Retrieve Additional Data" has two sub-options: "Retrieve issue data" retrieves additional data such as a process memory dump, while "Retrieve related files" initiates retrieval of attack-related files — mainly the executables. These are distinct operations targeting different artifact types.

questions.question: Under which navigation path do you create a new Issue Starring Configuration?
options: Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Featured Fields
Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
correct_answers: Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues
questions.correct_answer: Cases & Issues > Case Configuration > Starred Issues

questions.question: A Cortex list is described as a container for storing data. In which two places can lists be primarily accessed during a playbook? (Choose two.)
options: Via the Incident Response > Investigations menu
Via the Schema tab on the XQL Search page

questions.question: Which navigation path is used to create and manage lists in the Cortex console?

questions.question: An analyst wants to append a single new IP address to an existing list without overwriting the other entries. Which CLI command should they use?
questions.correct_answer: addToList
questions.explanation: `addToList` appends single or multiple items to a specified list without overwriting existing content. `setList` overwrites the entire list, `getList` retrieves content, and `appendList` does not exist as a command in the source material.

questions.question: Which command overwrites the entire content of an existing list with new data?
questions.correct_answer: setList
questions.explanation: The `setList` command takes `listName` and `listData` arguments and overwrites items in the specified list. This is distinct from `addToList` (which appends) and `createList` (which creates a new list from scratch).

questions.question: Which CLI command retrieves the content of a specified list when used in the War Room?
questions.correct_answer: getList

questions.question: On the Lists page, which action uses the vertical ellipsis menu?

The page timer icon (next to + Add a List) views version history of all lists, the cloud icon imports from a local file, and the time arrow icon reverts to a prior saved version of a specific list.

questions.question: Which content type is NOT listed as a supported format when creating a list in Cortex?
questions.correct_answer: CSV
questions.explanation: The source lists the following content types in the drop-down when creating a list: Text, Markdown, HTML, CSS, and JSON. CSV is not listed as a selectable content type in the list creation interface.

questions.question: A security analyst wants to import threat feed data into a list for use in IOC identification during case investigations. Which use case from the source material best describes this scenario?

While allow/block lists use similar mechanics, the IOC identification from external threat feed import maps directly to this use case.

questions.question: Which XQL stage creates or updates variables and fields but does NOT filter rows?
questions.correct_answer: alter
questions.explanation: The `alter` stage creates new variables or modifies existing ones. Crucially, it does not filter rows — it only changes values. The `filter` stage removes rows, `fields` selects columns, and `comp` aggregates.

questions.question: Consider the following query snippet. Why will it produce an error?
options: The `comp` stage does not support `count()` as an aggregate function.
The `filter` stage comes after the `comp` stage, violating stage ordering rules.
The `dataset` stage must be preceded by a `config` stage.
The `filter` stage cannot use string comparisons.
correct_answers: The `filter` stage comes after the `comp` stage, violating stage ordering rules.
questions.correct_answer: The `filter` stage comes after the `comp` stage, violating stage ordering rules.
questions.explanation: XQL enforces strict stage ordering. `filter` must precede `comp`. In the snippet, `comp` runs before `filter`, which is invalid. The correct order is: dataset → filter → alter → fields → comp → sort/limit.

questions.question: The `fields` stage has a side effect beyond selecting output columns. What is it?
options: It sorts results alphabetically by the first listed field.
It erases all fields and variables defined before it.
It applies a default filter removing null-valued rows.
It triggers an implicit `comp` aggregation on the selected fields.
correct_answers: It erases all fields and variables defined before it.
questions.correct_answer: It erases all fields and variables defined before it.
questions.explanation: The source states the `fields` stage "erases all the fields and variables defined before it — only the fields listed are kept." This is a critical behavior: any variables created by prior `alter` stages that are not explicitly listed in `fields` will not appear in the result.

questions.question: What does the following query return?
options: All raw event rows where event_type is FILE, NETWORK, or PROCESS, limited to 10.
The 10 agents with the highest count of FILE, NETWORK, or PROCESS events.
An error, because `in` is not a valid XQL operator in the filter stage.
The 10 most recent events across all event types, sorted descending.
correct_answers: The 10 agents with the highest count of FILE, NETWORK, or PROCESS events.
